thesis: Docusign (Nasdaq: DOCU), fiscal year ends Jan 31. Q2 FY27 10-Q (to 2026-07-31; first 100,000 of 109,469 characters read) and 2026-09-03 earnings release read. Revenue 875.7M (+9%), six months 1,706.0M (+9%), subscription 854.0M; GAAP operating margin 13.4% (non-GAAP 31.6%); Q2 FCF 295.8M (34%); RPO over 1 year 2.3B; customers over 300K ACV 1,296 from 1,137. Guide: Q3 revenue 886M to 890M, FY27 3,499M to 3,507M (+9%), non-GAAP operating margin 31.0% to 31.5%, ARR growth 8.5% to 9.0%. TTM revenue 3361M, net income 330M, FCF 1198M (OCF 1324M less PP&E 125M), SBC 606M, so FCF after SBC about 592M. Close 76.57 on 2026-11-18 x 186,902,452 shares (10-Q cover 2026-08-31) = 14.31B market cap = 43.4x TTM GAAP net income, FCF yield 8.4% (4.1% after SBC); cash and investments 990.4M, revolver 750M undrawn, no debt; EV about 13321M, EV/revenue 4.0x. Buybacks 624M in six months (TTM about 1.11B, near the full TTM FCF) with 2.1B authorization left; share count fell from 194.4M (2026-02-28) to 186.9M. The market is pricing a mature, 9% growth seat vendor facing AI substitution risk; the evidence for a different view is high cash conversion, a roughly 4% FCF yield after SBC and buybacks shrinking the share count about 4% in six months. Not shown to be mispriced: SBC is 18% of revenue and the stock has no peer or history comparison yet.
counterthesis: SBC of about 606M TTM is roughly half of FCF, so owner earnings are far below headline FCF; the FCF definition excludes about 176M TTM of capitalized software (part non-cash SBC). Growth is stuck near 9% and net retention and billings are undisclosed in the sections read. AI-native contract tools could pressure seats and pricing. Buybacks near 100% of FCF reduce flexibility; the effective tax rate near 36% for six months reflects SBC shortfalls. Management adjusted margins (31.6%) are not owner earnings.
invalidation: Invalidated if revenue growth falls below about 6% or ARR growth below 8%, if FCF after SBC falls under 3% of market cap without a lower price, if SBC rises above 20% of revenue, or if repurchases are debt funded while growth slows.
